title: What puts a local business in Google's map pack

media.alt: Slide 1 of 7. Headline: Why do three businesses get the map, and everyone else gets scrolled past? Below it, a simple map pack diagram: results 1, 2 and 3 in bold with pins, a dashed cut line, then results 4 and 5 faded.

Slide 2 of 7. Google ranks local results on three things: 1 Relevance, does your profile match the search; 2 Distance, how close are you to the searcher; 3 Prominence, how well known is your business. Google says there is no way to pay for a better local ranking.

Slide 3 of 7. Factor 1, Relevance: how closely your Business Profile matches what the person typed. Do this: pick the category that says exactly what you do, then fill every field: hours, services, attributes.

Slide 4 of 7. Factor 2, Distance: how far your business is from the person searching. Do this: make sure Google knows exactly where you are, with the full, correct address on your profile and your website.

Slide 5 of 7. Factor 3, Prominence: how well known you are, including links from other sites and your reviews and ratings. Do this: ask every happy customer for a Google review and reply to each one, then earn links from local sites.

Slide 6 of 7. Our client, in the top three. A framed screenshot of a Google search for Primary Care Ellenton, FL, showing three Places results; the third, Ellenton Family Practice Direct, 4.5 stars, 71 reviews, is boxed in orange. Real incognito search, Sept 24, nothing edited.
Slide 7 of 7. Want to show up where people look? K&A builds local search into every site. Recap: 1 Relevance, 2 Distance, 3 Prominence. ka-performancefl.com. Call Alex 904-210-1071.

Why do three businesses get the map, and everyone else gets scrolled past?
